deviations: Price, income and instruments taken in the dataset's CPI-deflated form (lnPRE, lny/lny2, lnPRE_papas_/lnPRE_aguav_/lnPRE_gascar_); the paper does not state whether prices are deflated. Income is only available deflated, so the price was kept in the same real terms.
Instruments use the dataset's imputed versions (missing household prices replaced by the period mean), so OLS and IV columns share one sample, as Table 2 reports identical N in all columns.
Retirement income (PENSIO_j) is not included as a control: it is in Table 1 but not in the control list of equation (4).

LIML implemented by hand (k-class with kappa = minimum eigenvalue); household-FE LIML estimated on within-demeaned data (FWL). Only point estimates are scored; cluster-robust SEs are printed as diagnostics.

Number of id counts all households in the estimation sample, including 586 that are left with a single observation after listwise deletion (fixest drops them from the FE fit; they do not affect the coefficients).
notes: Data: analysis data/data_to_run_DOFILE3.dta (read with haven). Sample: observations with the reform dummy T2 defined (Sept 2011-Mar 2014 interviews; 25,775 obs / 12,888 households, matching the paper's panel size), then listwise deletion on regression variables (mainly economic-situation missing for 4,445 obs and surface for 462) -> 20,872 obs, 10,729 households. Dependent variables lnc_ele and lng_ele (log annualised kWh and EUR). Regressors: T2, log real kWh price, log real income and its square, months since reform (dist), household size, rooms, m2, elderly, renting, building >25 yrs, urban, province capital, education (4), economic situation (3), municipality size (5), region (CCAA), quarter dummies, year dummies; household FE in cols 3/4/7/8; SEs clustered by household. Three exploratory runs (variable listing, tabulations, variable-definition checks) printed no RESULT lines. No author scripts or result files were opened.
